- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.8) and recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (e.g., <0.3) and recent prices are trending down.
- Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecast after recent price peaks — model tends to overreact and overshoot.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, reduce forecast magnitude by 5–10% to account for mean reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, cap forecast growth to avoid overfitting to recent trends.
- If sentiment history includes multiple high values followed by a drop, model should adjust downward bias in subsequent forecasts.
- When true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >10% gap), check if sentiment was bullish — if so, reduce forecast by 5–15% for next period.
- If forecast consistently exceeds true outcome by 5–10% over 3–5 periods, apply a downward bias correction of 2–5% per period.
